title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement of longer-run goals and policy strategy
主要内容: On January 25, 2012, the Federal Reserve issued a FOMC statement outlining its longer-run goals and policy strategy. The statement emphasized that inflation over the longer run is primarily determined by monetary policy. The Committee judged that inflation at a rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent with the Federal Reserve's statutory mandate. The goal is to keep longer-term inflation expectations firmly anchored, fostering price stability and moderate long-term interest rates. The maximum level of employment is largely determined by nonmonetary factors affecting the labor market. The Committee does not specify a fixed goal for employment, instead relying on assessments of maximum employment levels. FOMC participants' estimates of the longer-run normal rate of unemployment had a central tendency of 5.2 percent to 6.0 percent, unchanged from last January but higher than several years earlier. The Committee seeks to mitigate deviations of inflation from its longer-run goal and deviations of employment from its assessments of maximum levels.
